name: Super League 1
content:
The Super League Greece is the top professional football division in Greece and represents the highest level of the country’s football league system. It was officially formed in 2006, replacing the long-standing Alpha Ethniki, and brings together the strongest clubs in Greek football. The competition is organized under the Greek football association and features clubs that also compete in European tournaments.

The league has a regular season format where teams play each other home and away, followed by play-off rounds that decide the champion and European qualification spots. Over time, it has been shaped by strong rivalries between traditional clubs such as Olympiacos, Panathinaikos, AEK Athens, and PAOK. The league also includes promotion and relegation with the second division, making performance each season highly competitive.

Before the creation of the Super League in 2006, Greek top-flight football was known as the Alpha Ethniki, which itself evolved from earlier national championships dating back to the 1920s. A major structural change happened in 2019 when the second-tier Football League system was reorganized and the pyramid below the top division was reshaped, strengthening the modern league structure and improving competitiveness across divisions.

name: Greek Cup
content:
The Greek Football Cup is the main national knockout football competition in Greece and is considered the second most important domestic tournament after the league championship. It was first established in 1931 and is organized by the Hellenic Football Federation. The competition includes clubs from different levels of Greek football, with top-tier teams typically joining in the later stages.

The tournament has a long and eventful history, including changes to its format over time. Traditionally, it follows a single-elimination structure, although in some periods two-legged ties were used in the knockout rounds. The Cup is known for producing dramatic matches and occasional upsets, where lower-division teams challenge and sometimes eliminate top Super League clubs.

A major historical issue mentioned in the competition’s past is the 1962 final, which was not properly concluded due to incidents and was never replayed, leaving no official winner that year. Over time, the competition introduced penalties, standardized rules, and more modern formats to avoid such situations. Today, it remains a key national trophy and an important route for clubs to qualify for European competitions.
